question: Violence against rescue and emergency workers has risen sharply in recent years. Interventions in high-risk areas are increasingly dangerous, and emergency workers are often required to respond to attacks such as shootings, stabbings and bombings. This raises serious concerns for the safety of our emergency service providers.

Russia’s aggression against Ukraine has further exposed these risks, with emergency responders being deliberately targeted. These circumstances require them to wear bulletproof vests and helmets to perform their duties. Regulation (EU) 2016/4251 sets out the current EU-level requirements for PPE. A derogation is provided for PPE designed for use by the armed forces or in the maintenance of law and order.

The reason for the derogation is that PPE designed for these purposes might not include the CE marking required by this regulation. However, rescue and emergency workers are not included in the derogation. This limits the possibilities for protecting workers in this field. Can the Commission therefore clarify: 1.
Whether it intends to amend Regulation (EU) 2016/425 to extend the derogation to cover PPE designed for use by rescue and emergency services?
What the time frame will be for this urgent update to the existing regulation?

Regulation (EU) 2016/425 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on personal protective equipment and repealing Council Directive 89/686/EEC (OJ L 81, 31.3.2016, p. 51, http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/425/oj). 1
